pr_body:
Fixes #20497 .

If merged, this PR should also be backported to 3.0 as this aligns the long-standing documentation for (the return value of) `EVP_PKEY(_get)_id` with its implementation (in the presence of provider-based EVP_PKEY algorithms).
pr_comments: Hmmm....the CI failures look relevant

> Hmmm....the CI failures look relevant

Yup. Problem found: In #19312 I did [work around the (now considered by us incorrect) retval of EVP_PKEY_get_id](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/931369429564b5a9bb09711de8e885fef546a0ac/ssl/t1_lib.c#L1843-L1857). Fixed in https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/20501/commits/47675ee42be2842bc5ecdff1c2725dbd4ec46088. Nice that "my own" tls-provider test found it :)

> @levitte is this correct? I see EVP_PKEY_KEYMGMT is a special case defined as -1

Yes, this is correct.  `NID_undef` is zero, and already signifies that the `EVP_PKEY` is unassigned (has no value), and that's hardly the case for an `EVP_PKEY` that's populated from a provider.  Therefore, another value was necessary, outside of the "normal" range of NIDs.

>  Therefore, another value was necessary, outside of the "normal" range of NIDs.

All right then -- that brings us to the core of the issue (also see https://github.com/openssl/openssl/issues/20497#issuecomment-1465968208): Should 
a) `EVP_PKEY_KEYMGMT` be documented (and used internally and externally as) a permitted return value for `EVP_PKEY_get_id` or 
b) should this not be done (retaining full backwards compatibility for code using the retval documentation for `EVP_PKEY_id` (Only 0/NID_undef or NIDs > 0)?

Option a) would possibly/probably require code changes in OpenSSL "consuming" apps -- which might be undesirable. Option b) would hide this -- possibly undesirable as well, e.g., if an app would like to know the algorithm name, for which `EVP_PKEY_get0_type_name` is a much better alternative in the presence of providers/OpenSSL3.

A third option might be "splitting" the APIs: `EVP_PKEY_get_id` would add `EVP_PKEY_KEYMGMT` as a permitted retval, while `EVP_PKEY_id` would not. That way, no problems would happen in code not aware of the new retval, e.g., if using it as input to `OBJ_nid2sn`. The current simple #define equating the two methods would need to be changed, of course.

Personally, I'd find the third option most appealing. Opinions, @levitte @mattcaswell @paulidale ?
Sorry, @baentsch, you're last comment wasn't visible to me when I wrote my review

> Sorry, @baentsch, you're last comment wasn't visible to me when I wrote my review

ACK. Would you want to add a comment on option c) above? Otherwise I'll proceed with option a) as seems to be the jist of your latest comment, @levitte . Just FYI, this will necessitate changes to "downstream" code like [this in OpenVPN](https://github.com/OpenVPN/openvpn/blob/838474145933199a62d1f59fbc2df14e4fbd57f3/src/openvpn/ssl_openssl.c#L2085-L2086).

> > Therefore, another value was necessary, outside of the "normal" range of NIDs.
> 
> All right then -- that brings us to the core of the issue (also see [#20497 (comment)](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/issues/20497#issuecomment-1465968208)): Should a) `EVP_PKEY_KEYMGMT` be documented (and used internally and externally as) a permitted return value for `EVP_PKEY_get_id` or b) should this not be done (retaining full backwards compatibility for code using the retval documentation for `EVP_PKEY_id` (Only 0/NID_undef or NIDs > 0)?
> 
> Option a) would possibly/probably require code changes in OpenSSL "consuming" apps -- which might be undesirable. Option b) would hide this -- possibly undesirable as well, e.g., if an app would like to know the algorithm name, for which `EVP_PKEY_get0_type_name` is a much better alternative in the presence of providers/OpenSSL3.
> 
> A third option might be "splitting" the APIs: `EVP_PKEY_get_id` would add `EVP_PKEY_KEYMGMT` as a permitted retval, while `EVP_PKEY_id` would not. That way, no problems would happen in code not aware of the new retval, e.g., if using it as input to `OBJ_nid2sn`. The current simple #define equating the two methods would need to be changed, of course.
> 
> Personally, I'd find the third option most appealing. Opinions, @levitte @mattcaswell @paulidale ?

I'd would rather not use option *b*, because that return value is confusing.  Would `NID_undef` mean that the `EVP_PKEY` is unassigned, or is assigned a provider based key?  How would anyone know?  Should I assign a value or not?

I would rather fix the documentation for clarity.  Option *a* was the intent in that regard.

As for the third option, this means changing something that's already clearly documented:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/931369429564b5a9bb09711de8e885fef546a0ac/doc/man3/EVP_PKEY_set1_RSA.pod?plain=1#L203-L207

So I'm not at all sure that your idea is as easy as you seem to imagine.  Note: *I'm not completely against the idea*, but the ramifications are unclear to me.

Also, note that `EVP_PKEY_type()` and `EVP_PKEY_get_base_id()` (which are really one and the same) does things a bit more like you want.

Finally, there's another point in the manual you've been looking at:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/931369429564b5a9bb09711de8e885fef546a0ac/doc/man3/EVP_PKEY_set1_RSA.pod?plain=1#L136-L143

It seems this is glossed over...

> It seems this is glossed over...

Don't get me wrong: I'm fine with what is documented there, actually any alternative; what concerns me is the original question that started this whole thing: 

What shall we do with this code pattern in downstream code: `OBJ_nid2sn(EVP_PKEY_id(pkey))`? 

It was completely OK in OpenSSL111 but now is wrong (and causes OpenVPN to quit execution when using (trying to display the name of) provider-based algorithms).

I'm absolutely fine doing a PR to OpenVPN to fix this (and update this PR to implement option a/stick to the current implementation of `EVP_PKEY_get_id`). It probably is the safest route to take given other OpenSSL consumers have adapted to the new behaviour of `EVP_PKEY_get_id`.

> > It seems this is glossed over...
> 
> Don't get me wrong: I'm fine with what is documented there, actually any alternative; what concerns me is the original question that started this whole thing:
> 
> What shall we do with this code pattern in downstream code: `OBJ_nid2sn(EVP_PKEY_id(pkey))`?

Ideally, I would have that replaced with `EVP_PKEY_get0_type_name(pkey)`, which will do the right thing regardless of where the contained key is.

I had hoped that we had written that up in the migration guide, but it seems we missed a spot 😖 
(and similarly, we should document there that something like `EVP_PKEY_type(pkey) == EVP_PKEY_RSA` should be replaced with `EVP_PKEY_is_a(pkey, "RSA")`)

> ...
> I'm absolutely fine doing a PR to OpenVPN to fix this (and update this PR to implement option a/stick to the current implementation of `EVP_PKEY_get_id`). It probably is the safest route to take given other OpenSSL consumers have adapted to the new behaviour of `EVP_PKEY_get_id`.

An adaptation to more modern methods would be a good thing.
OTC: needs to discuss the best method of solving this issue.

> > What shall we do with this code pattern in downstream code: `OBJ_nid2sn(EVP_PKEY_id(pkey))`?
> 
> Ideally, I would have that replaced with `EVP_PKEY_get0_type_name(pkey)`, which will do the right thing regardless of where the contained key is.

Another idea could be to have `OBJ_nid2sn()` and `OBJ_nid2ln()` detect -1 and return a generic string, so there's at least something to display.  I'm not very attached to that idea, but it would solve the immediate issue...  or rather push the issue to someone wondering what that generic string means.

>  or rather push the issue to someone wondering what that generic string means.

:-) More seriously, if we pursue this, I'd suggest having that generic string point to the (properly amended) migration document. I'll do an OpenVPN PR regardless of how the discussion here ends.

BTW, I need to amend what I've said earlier.  We *do* make an effort to set the `EVP_PKEY` id to something sensible if there's a matching legacy implementation for the provider implementation that's being handled.  It happens in `EVP_PKEY_set_type_by_keymgmt()`:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/931369429564b5a9bb09711de8e885fef546a0ac/crypto/evp/p_lib.c#L1602-L1652

So I have been a bit too strict about the meaning of `EVP_PKEY_KEYMGMT` returned by `EVP_PKEY_id()`...  it will only be returned when libcrypto doesn't have a preconceived idea of the key type (in form of an internal legacy implementation, or in form of an ENGINE implementation).  What this means isn't only that there needs to exist an OBJ database entry for it, but there must also exist an `EVP_PKEY_ASN1_METHOD` instance that libcrypto knows about.
I have no idea for the moment how to document that in a good enough way for user consumption without going very much into internal details...

> I have no idea for the moment how to document that in a good enough way for user consumption without going very much into internal details...

I'd just say something like - `For provided EVP_PKEYs whose algorithms do not have an internal or engine-based implementation -1 is returned as the id.`

> I'd just say something like - For provided EVP_PKEYs whose algorithms do not have an internal or engine-based implementation -1 is returned as the id.

Are engines still supported in `master` (or worthwhile mentioning any more)? So might this be even shortened to 

> For EVP_PKEYs implemented by an [external provider](https://www.openssl.org/docs/manmaster/man7/provider.html), -1 (EVP_PKEY_KEYMGMT) is returned as the id.

? This might be improved further by clearly documenting prominently (and pointing to it in this case) the distinction between "external" and "internal" (providers and algorithms).

> Are engines still supported in `master` (or worthwhile mentioning any more)? So might this be even shortened to

They are still supported and will be until the 4.0 at the earliest.

> > I have no idea for the moment how to document that in a good enough way for user consumption without going very much into internal details...
> 
> I'd just say something like - `For provided EVP_PKEYs whose algorithms do not have an internal or engine-based implementation -1 is returned as the id.`

Not sure I'd have that being "internal", as I fully expect that everything surrounding `EVP_PKEY_ASN1_METHOD` will be removed, along with ENGINEs...  "internal" sounds more permanent, and we've used the term "legacy" elsewhere.

Of course, that removal will happen in 4.0 at the earliest

I do not see a reason why we couldn't return nid that translates to real OID for these internally implemented algorithms even after we remove engines. Or, if we do not want to, then we should deprecate EVP_PKEY_get_id ASAP. Because keeping the function but have it always return just 0 or -1 after the legacy code removal does not make any sense.

`EVP_PKEY_get_id()` could call `OBJ_create()` and return it's NID in the case of unknown.
No doubt this path is fraught with problems...

> 

That requires an OID, where does that come from? (We had some arguments about the OIDS  that are embedded in the OSSL_DISPATCH name aliases a while ago)

It requires and OID, a short name **or** a long name.  Any one of the three is sufficient to create a new object.  The algorithm was fetched by name so we can fill one of the names out.

I'd suggested using _provider:name_ to avoid the (unlikely) situation where two different providers both include algorithms with the same name yet are different.  Or not.
That solves the issue in this particular case.. It doesnt solve getting the OID.

If a provider does include something that looks like an OID as one of the algorithm's names, we could try to detect this and pass the OID into the creation function.  Guessing something might be an OID isn't too hard.  At least until somebody invents the _1.234_ KDF :grinning:

Please let me know whether you'd expect me to do sth right now; otherwise I'd expect to hear a proposal which way to go (a-c above or sth else entirely). @levitte: The OpenVPN update to make this a "non-issue" there is available: https://github.com/OpenVPN/openvpn/pull/278
I think we're still in the _decide how to do best do this_ phase.

t8m said:
> I do not see a reason why we couldn't return nid that translates to real OID for these internally implemented algorithms even after we remove engines.

So you'd keep the diverse `EVP_PKEY_ASN1_ALGORITHM` instances around in libcrypto...  forever?  (I assume stripped down to just be a NID reference, but otherwise pretty useless).  Mind you, I'm not proposing that these get removed as soon as ENGINEs, exactly because they still have this use.

> Or, if we do not want to, then we should deprecate EVP_PKEY_get_id ASAP. Because keeping the function but have it always return just 0 or -1 after the legacy code removal does not make any sense.

I would agree with deprecating such functions in the next iteration.  So, not for removal in 4.0 or whenever we plan on getting rid of ENGINEs, but perhaps deprecate them when that removal happens.  (or well, I actually don't mind going more radical and deprecate them nownownow, but I doubt everyone agrees)

Historical note: By the time 3.0 was almost ready for beta, we chose a level of caution with deprecations, though.  Plus, there are other functionality that dearly needs fixing / changing / adapting to a provider world first.

I assume that magically parsing out the OID from the algorithm name string and auto-creating an OBJ for it (an considering the current mechanism, a stripped down `EVP_PKEY_ASN1_METHOD` instance?) is going to be regarded as a new feature, i.e. goes into master only.  This doesn't solve anything for 3.1 or 3.0.

I would deprecate them only if we decide to deprecate all functions related to NIDs.

Given we added the obj callbacks to the provider API I assume this is not going to happen soon.

> I would deprecate them only if we decide to deprecate all functions related to NIDs.
> 
> Given we added the obj callbacks to the provider API I assume this is not going to happen soon.

That was supposed to be an interim measure.  See https://github.com/openssl/openssl/issues/15624#issuecomment-855653176 and discussions around that.  Unfortunately, it seems we failed to mark it as such (something I asked for: https://github.com/openssl/openssl/issues/15624#issuecomment-855682038)

**OTC: This should not be merged. We instead want a documentation improvement of the EVP_PKEY_get_id return value and mention in the migration guide that EVP_PKEY_get0_type_name() is the replacement. The same documentation fix should be done for equivalent functions for ciphers and digests.**
Note: this can't be merged *as it currently stands*.  @baentsch, it's at your discretion to change this PR or to create a new one for documentation changes, if you're still willing to do the work.

Our reasoning for the decision is that `EVP_PKEY_KEYMGMT` is an already existing return value for algorithms that exist in provider form only, and some applications may rely on that value being returned for those cases.  Making changes that have `EVP_PKEY_get_id()` return a "valid" NID in all cases could become a breaking change just as much.

In the weighing of alternatives, which all are potentially painful, and weighing in that that we do want to deprecate public NID usage going forward, the OTC made a choice.
ACK. The problem the code change would have fixed is anyway already resolved downstream: I'll revert the code change and amend the documentation as per the above.

> Final nits and I'll approve.

... and I'll re-approve
@t8m Done as per the above.

24 hours has passed since 'approval: done' was set, but this PR has failing CI tests.  Once the tests pass it will get moved to 'approval: ready to merge' automatically, alternatively please review and set the label manually.

> alternatively please review and set the label manually.

Could someone please do so? The failing CI tests (Windows only) very likely have no relation to the PR contents.

I've smashed all commit into one, and modified the commit message to this:

```
Update the EVP_PKEY_get_id documentation

The documentation didn't mention the development where EVP_PKEY_get_id()
returns a negative value for provider-only implementations, and the
migration guide didn't mention how to cope with that.

Fixes #20497
```

Merged

issue_context.title: EVP_PKEY_(get_)id not returning an OID (for provider PKEYs)
issue_context.body:
The `master`[documentation for `EVP_PKEY_get_id`](https://www.openssl.org/docs/man3.0/man3/EVP_PKEY_id.html) (and thus for the old API `EVP_PKEY_id`) is documented to return an _OID_:

> EVP_PKEY_get_id() returns the actual OID associated with pkey. 

Is this really correct? It rather seems to return a NID (or doesn't "OID" in this context refer to an X.509 OID but rather to an "OpenSSL internal object ID"?). In that case some clarification wrt "OID" may be in order (Apologies if I missed this somewhere). 

The result is always used as a NID anyway. The one use that causes acute problems is [here](https://github.com/OpenVPN/openvpn/blob/838474145933199a62d1f59fbc2df14e4fbd57f3/src/openvpn/ssl_openssl.c#L2085-L2086): 

The issue is that a provider-based PKEY always causes `EVP_PKEY(_get)_id` to return -1 -- which is rather "suboptimal" for code interested in outputting the (SN) name of the algorithm. 

Or asked another way: How should an OpenSSL consumer (like OpenVPN) obtain the name (and/or NID) of the algorithm underlying a PKEY if that PKEY is provider-based? Ideally, it shouldn't know/have to worry about this "OpenSSL internal implementation detail", right?

In the OpenVPN use case, the problem is made worse by OpenSSL setting an error state due to the API call sequence `EVP_PKEY_get_id`-> `OBJ_nid2sn`: This causes the whole OpenVPN system to fail as OpenSSL reported an error:

> OpenSSL: error:04000065:object identifier routines::unknown nid

but only when logging is set too high (trying to obtain the algorithm name as per the above). Really surprising to users. Does an error state have to be set if a "provider-based" PKEY is examined?
comments:
> Is this really correct?

No, it's a NID. Usually there's a one-to-one correspondence from NID to OID (`OBJ_nid2oid`), so I guess that's where the confusion comes from.

> Or asked another way: How should an OpenSSL consumer (like OpenVPN) obtain the name (and/or NID) of the algorithm underlying a PKEY if that PKEY is provider-based? Ideally, it shouldn't know/have to worry about this "OpenSSL internal implementation detail", right?

If we're talking about a name for human consumption, does `EVP_PKEY_get0_description` do the trick?

> No, it's a NID. 

OK, then I'd suggest a documentation update (will do so if no-one jumps at this). I'd also add the correction that the retval from that function may actually be -1 (not just NID_undef or positive NID as currently documented) thus indicating a provided key. Would it be sensible to then also directly point to `EVP_PKEY_get0_type_name` for that case? 

> does EVP_PKEY_get0_description do the trick?

No, that also returns NULL (but that might arguably be changed by the provider implementation). But it would not solve the issue for OpenVPN: Are you saying [the code there](https://github.com/OpenVPN/openvpn/blob/838474145933199a62d1f59fbc2df14e4fbd57f3/src/openvpn/ssl_openssl.c#L2085-L2086) must be updated to support providers? Adding a call to `EVP_PKEY_get0_type_name` would be sufficient if `EVP_PKEY_(get_)id` returns -1.

If so, do you recommend a "standard way" how to utilize OpenSSLv3 APIs (such as `EVP_PKEY_get0_type_name`) in "consumer code" (like OpenVPN)? Something like `#if OPENSSL_VERSION >= 0x30000000L`?

> may actually be -1 (not just NID_undef or positive NID as currently documented)

That is really unfortunate. Arguably that's a bug. We should either fix it, or fix the documentation. I worry whether it might be too late to actually fix it though??? Maybe applications already rely on this. Not sure.

> Are you saying [the code there](https://github.com/OpenVPN/openvpn/blob/838474145933199a62d1f59fbc2df14e4fbd57f3/src/openvpn/ssl_openssl.c#L2085-L2086) must be updated to support providers?

Looks like it. It should still be ok if its a provider supplied sig alg that OpenSSL already knows about - but if it is completely unknown to OpenSSL its just not going to work.

> Adding a call to EVP_PKEY_get0_type_name would be sufficient if EVP_PKEY_(get_)id returns -1.

Shouldn't you be able to just always call `EVP_PKEY_get0_type_name` in OpenSSL 3.0 (and not call `EVP_PKEY_get_id` at all)? That should work even for legacy keys.

`OPENSSL_VERSION_NUMBER` can be checked for conditional compilation where support for older APIs is required. See:

https://www.openssl.org/docs/man3.0/man3/OPENSSL_VERSION_NUMBER.html

Note that page describes numerous macros for checking the version number - but many of those were introduced in 3.0. `OPENSSL_VERSION_NUMBER` can reliably be used for older versions.

> That is really unfortunate. Arguably that's a bug. We should either fix it, or fix the documentation. I worry whether it might be too late to actually fix it though??? Maybe applications already rely on this.

Their fault if they do. It's clearly documented. I'd suggest fixing the code instead. It would also solve the "downstream" OpenVPN problem: The whole code causing the problem would not trigger again if the retval of `EVP_PKEY_get_id` were 0 (or a real NID): https://github.com/OpenVPN/openvpn/blob/838474145933199a62d1f59fbc2df14e4fbd57f3/src/openvpn/ssl_openssl.c#L2083-L2107

As simple as

```
diff --git a/crypto/evp/p_lib.c b/crypto/evp/p_lib.c
index 554fad927c..6477594017 100644
--- a/crypto/evp/p_lib.c
+++ b/crypto/evp/p_lib.c
@@ -982,7 +982,7 @@ int EVP_PKEY_type(int type)
 
 int EVP_PKEY_get_id(const EVP_PKEY *pkey)
 {
-    return pkey->type;
+    return pkey->type > 0 ? pkey->type : NID_undef;
 }
```

OK to PR?
Let's have a PR for it. We can gather more opinion there.
